members.summary: Frozen configuration for the VQ-VAE family.
members.extended:
Defaults reproduce the image experiments of van den Oord et al., 2017
(Section 4.1): two stride-2 encoder convolutions with a 4x4 window,
two residual blocks, 256 hidden units throughout, a `512 x 256`
codebook, and `commitment_cost = 0.25`.

parameters.name: sample_size
parameters.description:
Input spatial resolution.  Inherited from
`GenerativeModelConfig`.  Must be divisible by
`2 ** num_downsample_layers`.

parameters.name: in_channels
parameters.description: Input image channels.

parameters.name: out_channels
parameters.description:
Reconstruction channels.  Must equal `in_channels`: the
reconstruction loss compares the decoder's output with the input.

parameters.name: act_fn
parameters.description:
Trunk activation.  The paper uses ReLU throughout, which is why
this family overrides the generative-domain default of `"silu"`.

parameters.name: num_embeddings
parameters.description: Codebook size $K$ — the number of discrete latent codes.

parameters.name: embedding_dim
parameters.description:
Code dimension $D$.  The encoder's final projection emits
this many channels so encoder outputs and codebook entries live in
the same space.

parameters.name: hidden_channels
parameters.description: Width of the encoder / decoder trunk.

parameters.name: num_downsample_layers
parameters.description:
Number of stride-2 convolutions.  The latent grid is
`sample_size / 2 ** num_downsample_layers` on a side.

parameters.name: num_residual_layers
parameters.description:
Number of residual blocks after the downsampling stack (and,
mirrored, before the decoder's upsampling stack).

parameters.name: residual_hidden_channels
parameters.description: Inner width of each residual block's 3x3 convolution.

parameters.name: commitment_cost
parameters.description: The coefficient $\beta$ weighting the commitment term.

parameters.name: recon_loss
parameters.description:
Reconstruction likelihood — Gaussian (`"mse"`) or Bernoulli
(`"bce"`, for data in `[0, 1]`).

examples:
>>> from lucid.models.generative.vqvae import VQVAEConfig
>>> cfg = VQVAEConfig(sample_size=32)
>>> cfg.latent_grid_size
(8, 8)
>>> cfg.num_embeddings, cfg.embedding_dim
(512, 256)
notes:
Reference: van den Oord, Vinyals, and Kavukcuoglu, *"Neural Discrete
Representation Learning"*, NeurIPS, 2017 ([arXiv:1711.00937](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.00937)).

The paper reports a single image architecture rather than a table of
sized variants, so this family exposes one nominal factory rather than
`_small` / `_base` / `_large` siblings.  Scale it by overriding
the fields above at `create_model` time.

The paper's Appendix A.1 also describes an exponential-moving-average
alternative to the codebook loss.  That variant changes how the
codebook is *updated* rather than what the network computes, so it
belongs to a training loop rather than to the architecture, and is not
modelled here.

attributes.name: latent_grid_size
attributes.description:
Spatial `(H, W)` of the discrete latent field, derived from
`sample_size` and `num_downsample_layers`.

members.name: VQVAEForImageGeneration

methods.name: generate
methods.signature: generate(n_samples: int = 1, device: str | None = None)
methods.summary: Sample `n_samples` images from the uniform codebook prior.
methods.extended: Draws an index field uniformly over $[0, K)$ and decodes it.

parameters.name: n_samples
parameters.description: Number of images to draw.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description:
Device to sample on.  `None` resolves to the device the
model's parameters already live on.

returns.description:
`samples` of shape `(n_samples, out_channels, H, W)`,
squashed through a sigmoid when `recon_loss="bce"` so the
result matches the space `forward` reports.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.generative.vqvae import VQVAEConfig
>>> from lucid.models.generative.vqvae import VQVAEForImageGeneration
>>> cfg = VQVAEConfig(sample_size=32, hidden_channels=16,
...                   residual_hidden_channels=16, embedding_dim=8,
...                   num_embeddings=32)
>>> VQVAEForImageGeneration(cfg).eval().generate(2).samples.shape
(2, 3, 32, 32)
notes:
This is the *training-time* prior — uniform is what makes the KL
term the constant $\log K$ and drops it from the objective.
It is not the paper's generative prior, which is a PixelCNN fit
over the latent grid afterwards, so these samples are expected to
be incoherent.  Fitting such a prior is a separate model over
`VQVAEModel.encode_indices` output.

members.summary: VQ-VAE with the full training objective and a codebook sampler.
members.extended:
Wraps `VQVAEModel` with the three-term objective of van den
Oord et al., 2017 — reconstruction, codebook, and
$\beta$-weighted commitment — and a convenience sampler.

`forward(x)` returns a `VQVAEOutput` carrying the
reconstruction, the quantised latent, the integer code field, the
codebook perplexity, and all four loss tensors.

Under `recon_loss="bce"` the decoder emits logits, which is what the
Bernoulli likelihood needs; `out.sample` and `generate().samples`
are squashed through a sigmoid so every reconstruction handed back
lives in the same `[0, 1]` space as the input, while the loss is
still computed from the raw logits.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description:
Hyperparameters.  `config.commitment_cost` is the $\beta$
coefficient; `config.recon_loss` selects the likelihood.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.generative.vqvae import (
...     VQVAEConfig, VQVAEForImageGeneration,
... )
>>> cfg = VQVAEConfig(sample_size=32, hidden_channels=32,
...                   residual_hidden_channels=32, embedding_dim=16,
...                   num_embeddings=64)
>>> model = VQVAEForImageGeneration(cfg).eval()
>>> x = lucid.randn((1, 3, 32, 32))
>>> out = model(x)
>>> out.sample.shape, out.loss.shape
((1, 3, 32, 32), ())
notes:
Reference: van den Oord, Vinyals, and Kavukcuoglu, *"Neural Discrete
Representation Learning"*, NeurIPS, 2017 ([arXiv:1711.00937](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.00937)).

Training objective:



$$
L = \log p(x \mid z_q(x))
    + \big\| \mathrm{sg}[z_e(x)] - e \big\|_2^2
    + \beta \big\| z_e(x) - \mathrm{sg}[e] \big\|_2^2 .
$$

**On `generate`.** The prior over the discrete latents is uniform
*during training* — that is the paper's choice, and it is why the KL
term is the constant $\log K$ and drops out of the objective.
`generate` samples from exactly that uniform prior, so it is
faithful to what this model was trained against, but it is not how
the paper produces its figures: there, a PixelCNN is fit over the
latent grid afterwards and sampled autoregressively.  Expect
incoherent images from the uniform sampler.  Fitting a prior is a
separate model over `encode_indices` output, deliberately outside
this family.

methods.name: quantize
methods.summary: Quantise an `(B, D, H', W')` latent field.
methods.extended:
`lucid.nn.VectorQuantizer` follows the framework's
trailing-axis convention, so the channel axis is moved last for
the lookup and moved back afterwards; the returned `quantized`
is in image layout, while `indices` is `(B, H', W')`.

methods.name: decode_indices

members.summary: Bare discrete-latent auto-encoder — encoder, codebook, decoder.
members.extended:
Implements the VQ-VAE of van den Oord, Vinyals, and Kavukcuoglu, 2017.
An image is encoded to a spatial field of continuous vectors, each
snapped to its nearest entry in a learned codebook of
`VQVAEConfig.num_embeddings` codes, and decoded back.  The
quantisation step is non-differentiable, so `forward` routes the
decoder's gradient onto the encoder with the straight-through
estimator.

This class computes no loss.  Use
`VQVAEForImageGeneration` for the training objective, or read
the `codebook_loss` / `commitment_loss` terms off the returned
`VQVAEOutput` and combine them yourself.

The pair `encode_indices` / `decode_indices` is the
tokeniser interface: images in, an integer field out, and back again.
Downstream discrete models over the latent grid — the paper's own
PixelCNN prior among them — consume exactly that.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description:
Hyperparameters controlling image shape, trunk width, codebook
size, and the commitment coefficient.  See `VQVAEConfig`.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.generative.vqvae import VQVAEConfig, VQVAEModel
>>> cfg = VQVAEConfig(sample_size=32, hidden_channels=32,
...                   residual_hidden_channels=32, embedding_dim=16,
...                   num_embeddings=64)
>>> model = VQVAEModel(cfg).eval()
>>> x = lucid.randn((1, 3, 32, 32))
>>> out = model(x)
>>> out.sample.shape, out.indices.shape
((1, 3, 32, 32), (1, 8, 8))
notes:
Reference: van den Oord, Vinyals, and Kavukcuoglu, *"Neural Discrete
Representation Learning"*, NeurIPS, 2017 ([arXiv:1711.00937](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.00937)).

The straight-through estimator used here is



$$
z_q^{\mathrm{st}} = z_e + \mathrm{sg}\!\big[z_q - z_e\big],
$$

which equals $z_q$ in the forward pass and has the identity
Jacobian with respect to $z_e$ in the backward pass.

attributes.name: encoder
attributes.description: Strided-conv encoder emitting `(B, embedding_dim, H', W')`.

attributes.name: quantizer
attributes.description:
Core-API codebook layer holding `(num_embeddings,
embedding_dim)` entries.

attributes.name: decoder
attributes.description:
Transposed-conv decoder mapping the quantised field back to image

members.summary: Forward output of the discrete-latent auto-encoder.
examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.generative.vqvae import (
...     VQVAEConfig, VQVAEForImageGeneration,
... )
>>> cfg = VQVAEConfig(sample_size=32, hidden_channels=16,
...                   residual_hidden_channels=16, embedding_dim=8,
...                   num_embeddings=32)
>>> out = VQVAEForImageGeneration(cfg).eval()(lucid.randn((4, 3, 32, 32)))
>>> out.sample.shape, out.indices.shape
((4, 3, 32, 32), (4, 8, 8))

attributes.name: latent
attributes.description:
Quantised latent field $z_q(x)$ shaped
`(B, embedding_dim, H', W')`, carrying the straight-through
gradient path back to the encoder.

attributes.name: indices
attributes.description:
Codebook assignment per spatial position, shaped `(B, H', W')`
with `int64` dtype and values in `[0, num_embeddings)`.  This
is the discrete token field a downstream prior would model.

attributes.name: perplexity
attributes.description:
Scalar $\exp(-\sum_k p_k \log p_k)$ over the batch's
codebook usage histogram.  Ranges over `[1, num_embeddings]`;
a value collapsing toward 1 means the codebook has died down to a
handful of live entries.

attributes.name: loss
attributes.description:
Total objective — `recon_loss + codebook_loss + beta *
commitment_loss`.  `None` on the bare
`VQVAEModel`, which does not build a loss.

attributes.name: codebook_loss
attributes.description:
$\| \mathrm{sg}[z_e] - e \|_2^2$ — moves the codebook
toward the encoder outputs assigned to it.

attributes.name: commitment_loss
attributes.description:
$\| z_e - \mathrm{sg}[e] \|_2^2$ — moves the encoder
toward the entry it selected.  Reported *unweighted*; the
$\beta$ scaling is applied only inside `loss`.

members.name: vqvae
members.summary: Construct a VQ-VAE trunk — encoder, codebook, decoder, no loss.
members.extended:
Discrete-latent auto-encoder following van den Oord, Vinyals, and
Kavukcuoglu, 2017, Section 4.1: two stride-2 convolutions with a 4x4
window, two pre-activation residual blocks, 256 hidden units
throughout, and a `512 x 256` codebook.  At the default
`sample_size=32` the latent grid is `8 x 8`.

Use `VQVAEModel.encode_indices` and
`VQVAEModel.decode_indices` for the tokeniser interface — an
image in, an integer code field out, and back.

parameters.name: pretrained
parameters.description:
No weights are published for this family; passing `True` raises
rather than returning a randomly initialised model.

parameters.name: **overrides
parameters.description:
Optional `VQVAEConfig` field overrides (e.g.
`sample_size=128` for the paper's ImageNet setting,
`num_embeddings=...`, `commitment_cost=...`) forwarded into
the underlying config.

returns.description:
VQ-VAE trunk configured with the paper defaults and any
overrides.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.generative.vqvae import vqvae
>>> model = vqvae().eval()
>>> x = lucid.randn((1, 3, 32, 32))
>>> out = model(x)
>>> out.sample.shape, out.indices.shape
((1, 3, 32, 32), (1, 8, 8))
notes:
Reference: van den Oord, Vinyals, and Kavukcuoglu, *"Neural Discrete
Representation Learning"*, NeurIPS, 2017 ([arXiv:1711.00937](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.00937)).

Quantisation snaps each spatial position of the encoder output to its
nearest codebook entry:



$$
z_q(x) = e_k,
\qquad
k = \arg\min_j \big\| z_e(x) - e_j \big\|_2 .
$$

members.name: vqvae_gen
members.summary: Construct a VQ-VAE with the full training objective and a sampler.
members.extended:
Same trunk as `vqvae`, wrapped with the three-term objective of
van den Oord et al., 2017 — reconstruction, codebook, and
$\beta$-weighted commitment — plus a convenience sampler over
the uniform codebook prior.

parameters.name: pretrained
parameters.description:
No weights are published for this family; passing `True` raises
rather than returning a randomly initialised model.

parameters.name: **overrides
parameters.description:
Optional `VQVAEConfig` field overrides forwarded into the
underlying config.  Pass `recon_loss="bce"` for Bernoulli
likelihoods on `[0, 1]` data, or `commitment_cost=...` to
retune $\beta$.

returns.description: VQ-VAE wrapped with the full objective and prior sampler.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.generative.vqvae import vqvae_gen
>>> model = vqvae_gen().eval()
>>> x = lucid.randn((1, 3, 32, 32))
>>> out = model(x)
>>> out.sample.shape, out.perplexity.shape
((1, 3, 32, 32), ())
notes:
Reference: van den Oord, Vinyals, and Kavukcuoglu, *"Neural Discrete
Representation Learning"*, NeurIPS, 2017 ([arXiv:1711.00937](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.00937)).

Training objective:



$$
L = \log p(x \mid z_q(x))
    + \big\| \mathrm{sg}[z_e(x)] - e \big\|_2^2
    + \beta \big\| z_e(x) - \mathrm{sg}[e] \big\|_2^2 .
$$

`generate` samples the *uniform* prior the model was trained
against, not a learned one — the paper fits a PixelCNN over the latent
grid for its figures.  Samples from the uniform prior are expected to
be incoherent; see `VQVAEForImageGeneration`.

summary: VQ-VAE family — van den Oord, Vinyals & Kavukcuoglu, 2017.
citation: van den Oord, Aaron, Oriol Vinyals, and Koray Kavukcuoglu. "Neural Discrete Representation Learning." Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, vol. 30, 2017, pp. 6306-6315.
theory:
The Vector-Quantised Variational Auto-Encoder replaces the continuous
Gaussian bottleneck of a VAE with a **discrete** one.  An encoder
$z_e(x)$ maps an image to a spatial grid of $D$-dimensional
vectors, and each grid position is snapped to its nearest neighbour in
a learned codebook $e \in \mathbb{R}^{K \times D}$:



$$
q(z = k \mid x) =
    \begin{cases}
        1 & \text{if } k = \arg\min_j \| z_e(x) - e_j \|_2 \\
        0 & \text{otherwise},
    \end{cases}
\qquad
z_q(x) = e_k .
$$

The decoder then reconstructs from $z_q(x)$.  Because the
$\arg\min$ has zero gradient almost everywhere, training uses the
**straight-through estimator** — the forward pass carries the quantised
vector while the backward pass copies the decoder's gradient directly
onto the encoder output, which is implemented as
$z_q = z_e + \mathrm{sg}[z_q - z_e]$ with $\mathrm{sg}$
the stop-gradient operator.

The codebook receives no gradient from that path, so it is trained by
two additional terms.  The **codebook loss** pulls each selected entry
toward the encoder output it was matched to, and the **commitment
loss** pulls the encoder output toward the entry it chose, preventing
the encoder's output space from growing without bound.  The full
objective is



$$
L = \underbrace{\log p(x \mid z_q(x))}_{\text{reconstruction}}
    + \underbrace{\big\| \mathrm{sg}[z_e(x)] - e \big\|_2^2}
                _{\text{codebook}}
    + \beta \underbrace{\big\| z_e(x) - \mathrm{sg}[e] \big\|_2^2}
                _{\text{commitment}},
$$

with $\beta = 0.25$ in the paper's experiments.  Note the
asymmetry: the codebook term is unweighted because the codebook has no
other learning signal, while $\beta$ scales how strongly the
encoder is held to its current assignment.

Unlike a Gaussian VAE there is no KL term to anneal.  The prior over
the discrete latents is held **uniform** during training, which makes
its KL the constant $\log K$ and removes posterior collapse as a
failure mode entirely — the paper's central practical claim.  A
faithful *generative* prior is fit afterwards as a separate
autoregressive model (PixelCNN over the latent grid), so the
auto-encoder trained here is a representation learner and a discrete
tokeniser rather than a stand-alone sampler.  That tokeniser role is
what later made the architecture load-bearing across discrete
generative modelling.
